title: WSPR Logger – User guide
description: How to read and use the page: WSPR in a nutshell, the live map and its layers (propagation, MUF graph, solar conditions, reporter list, histogram and plot, day/night), the History Player, the History and Statistics pages, every chart of the Propagation Analysis page explained with examples from this station's data, the WPRS page, questions you can answer, limitations and a quick reference.

title: WSPR Logger – Mobile app user guide
description: The phone view at /app: opening it and adding it to the home screen, the top bar and the ☰ menu, and each of its nine views — Live map, Now, Reporters, MUF graph, Replay, History, Statistics, Analysis and WPRS — with their options, how the app keeps itself up to date, where the parts of the full page are, and a quick reference.

title: WPRS – two-page summary
description: The WPRS paper in two pages: how a GPS-equipped 200 mW WSPR transmitter on a car reports its position over HF, the key measurements of the 2024–2026 seasons (availability, confirmation, accuracy, reach at lower power), where the technique fits and practical tips.

title: WPRS – Whisper Position Reporting System
description: How a 200 mW WSPR transmitter with GPS and a car-roof 14 MHz antenna reports its position over HF without any mobile or VHF coverage; design, position accuracy, availability, power and battery measurements, and a comparison of the 2024, 2025 and 2026 seasons.

title: Twenty-metre WSPR propagation study
description: Scientific analysis of three summer seasons (2024–2026, 495 days) of WSPR data: diurnal and seasonal patterns, geography, long-distance windows, season-to-season comparison and the effect of MUF, K-index and solar flux (2026).
